$comment: PERMISSION MODE. The routines here run unattended in an ephemeral cloud container on a
schedule, with no human in the session. A permission prompt in that setting has nobody to
answer it, so the run does not fail, it WEDGES: it holds the container open until the
container is reclaimed, and the day's work is lost with no error anyone sees. bypassPermissions
is what keeps an unattended run finishing. It is not the thing containing the blast radius.
The containment is ownership.yaml, the CI guards, and the fact that docs/ is regenerated
rather than edited: a run can only write inside its own lane, and only a maintainer session
can change what the lanes are. Owner decision, 2026-08-11.

hooks.command: python3 -c "import importlib,subprocess,sys; need=[p for m,p in [('yaml','pyyaml'),('requests','requests')] if not importlib.util.find_spec(m)]; subprocess.run([sys.executable,'-m','pip','install','--break-system-packages','-q',*need]) if need else None" 2>/dev/null || true
